headline: Stoppage-time strike: Canada reach World Cup last 16 for the first time
summary: Stephen Eustaquio's late long-range goal secures a 1-0 victory over South Africa in the tournament's first knockout match.
details: Canada made history on Sunday by reaching the World Cup last 16 for the first time. A dramatic stoppage-time strike from distance by Stephen Eustaquio secured a 1-0 win over South Africa.

The match, held at Los Angeles Stadium, remained a tense, scoreless deadlock for most of the game. Eustaquio finally broke the tie by hammering the ball past goalkeeper Ronwen Williams in the closing moments.

Canada's path to the goal was fraught with frustration, including a denied penalty after a VAR review and several near-misses. Moise Bombito and Tajon Buchanan both had efforts blocked or saved in the first half.

South Africa appeared content to push the game into extra time and a penalty shootout, but they were unable to respond after the late goal. Canada's coach, Jesse Marsch, praised his players as 'Canadian heroes' for sticking to the plan.
Canada will now advance to face either the Netherlands or Morocco on July 4 in Houston to compete for a spot in the quarter-finals.
caption:
History made! 🇨🇦 Canada reaches the World Cup last 16 for the first time ever with a dramatic last-minute goal.

Canada made history on Sunday by reaching the World Cup last 16 for the first time. A dramatic stoppage-time strike from distance by Stephen Eustaquio secured a 1-0 win over South Africa.

The match, held at Los Angeles Stadium, remained a tense, scoreless deadlock for most of the game. Eustaquio finally broke the tie by hammering the ball past goalkeeper Ronwen Williams in the closing moments.

Canada's path to the goal was fraught with frustration, including a denied penalty after a VAR review and several near-misses. Moise Bombito and Tajon Buchanan both had efforts blocked or saved in the first half.

South Africa appeared content to push the game into extra time and a penalty shootout, but they were unable to respond after the late goal. Canada's coach, Jesse Marsch, praised his players as 'Canadian heroes' for sticking to the plan.

Canada will now advance to face either the Netherlands or Morocco on July 4 in Houston to compete for a spot in the quarter-finals.

headline_marked: Iran's [[Khamenei demands trial of US and Israeli leaders]] for child killing
headline: Iran's Khamenei demands trial of US and Israeli leaders for child killing
summary: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei calls for the prosecution of foreign leaders in national and international courts for alleged war crimes and aggression.
details: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has demanded the trial of US and Israeli leaders for the killing of children. The demand was made in a message posted on X (formerly Twitter) on Sunday.
Khamenei stated that those responsible for 'child killing, war crimes, and aggression' committed against Iran in 2025-26 should be held accountable in both domestic and international courts.
He argued that the public statements of US and Israeli leaders could be considered as confessions of these crimes.
The remarks were made on the anniversary of the death of former Chief Justice Ayatollah Mohammad Beheshti and other top political leaders killed in a 1981 bombing.
The reference to 2025 refers to a 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June 2025.

As a primary example of 'child killing,' Khamenei cited a US missile strike on the Shajareh Tayyebah Girls' Primary School in the city of Minab. On February 28, during the first day of the US-Iran war, the strike reportedly killed over 100 children.
Iranian authorities claim that more than 175 people, mostly children, including teachers, were killed in the school attack.
